title: Why do translators leave this famous word untranslated?

beats.narration: One of this book's most famous words is almost never translated. What does it actually say?
Most translations carry it straight over as a name. But listen to how this verse renders it. I have been commanded to be among those who submit. A verb. Something a person does.

The root is seen lam meem. In the oldest poetry every branch grows from one kernel, wholeness. A warrior comes home saalim, safe and intact. A sound horse is saleem, flawless. And handing something over, giving it up whole, is the same root's verb.

root.label: s-l-m
root.meaning: wholeness, safety, peace — and the handing-over of a thing, whole

beats.narration: Now hear its sister in this verse. When the ignorant address them, they answer with one word. Salaaman. Peace. The famous name and the greeting of peace are one root. To hand yourself over whole, and to be whole.
So it is not a label you inherit. It is a motion you make. Giving yourself over, whole, and finding wholeness on the other side of it.
